channel.title: Diogo Fitness: Learn
channel.description: Straight answers on training, eating and consistency from online fitness coach Diogo Camera.

item.title: Workout log: five columns that make overload work
item.dc:creator: Diogo Camera
item.description: What a workout log needs: exercise, weight, reps per set, reps in reserve and a note. A layout to copy on paper or in a notes app, and how to read it.

item.title: Rain by metro: average annual precipitation in 40 metros
item.dc:creator: Diogo Camera
item.description: NOAA's 1991–2020 average annual precipitation at a named weather station in 40 U.S. metros, and what a wet day changes in a training week: the walk, not the lifting.

item.title: How much weight to lift: let the reps decide
item.dc:creator: Diogo Camera
item.description: How much weight to lift: pick the reps first, then a weight that leaves two or three in reserve. Why charts miss, how beginners start, when to add weight.

item.title: How active is your city? CDC estimates for 27 U.S. cities
item.dc:creator: Diogo Camera
item.description: The CDC's PLACES estimates for 27 U.S. cities: adults with no leisure-time physical activity and adults reporting short sleep, with 95% ranges and how to read them.

item.title: Commute times by metro, and how to train around yours
item.dc:creator: Diogo Camera
item.description: The Census Bureau's average trip to work and work-from-home share for 40 U.S. metro areas, with margins of error, and where training fits around each.

item.title: A mobility routine for lifters: ten minutes for the range your lifts use
item.dc:creator: Diogo Camera
item.description: A ten-minute mobility routine for lifters (ankles, hips, upper back, shoulders), mobility vs flexibility in plain words, and what changes range over weeks.

item.title: Dumbbell vs barbell: what each does better, lift by lift
item.dc:creator: Diogo Camera
item.description: Dumbbell vs barbell for the bench, incline, shoulder press, row, RDL, curl and shrug: what the studies measured, what they found, and what they didn't test.

item.title: Core workout: what your squats already cover, and what to add
item.dc:creator: Diogo Camera
item.description: A core workout for people who lift: what squats and deadlifts already train, what they miss, and four exercises to add after your main lifts, gym or home.

item.title: Cool-down after a workout: what it does, and what it doesn't
item.dc:creator: Diogo Camera
item.description: Do you need a cool-down after lifting? What studies of cool-downs and stretching after exercise found, what they didn't, and a short one if you like it.

item.title: Arm workout: count what the compounds already did
item.dc:creator: Diogo Camera
item.description: An arm workout that counts what presses and rows already give your biceps and triceps, then adds a curl and an overhead triceps extension. Gym or home.

item.title: Winter cold by metro: January lows in 48 big metros
item.dc:creator: Diogo Camera
item.description: NOAA's 1991–2020 average January low at weather stations in 48 big U.S. metros, and what cold, dark months change in a training week: the walk, not the lifting.

item.title: Supersets: two exercises, one rest
item.dc:creator: Diogo Camera
item.description: What supersets and drop sets are, the three ways to pair exercises, what the research says about time and gains, and when to leave them out of your workout.

item.title: Summer heat by metro: 90-degree days and July highs
item.dc:creator: Diogo Camera
item.description: NOAA's 1991–2020 normals at weather stations in 48 big U.S. metros: days a year at or above 90 F, the average July high, and when to move outdoor training.

item.title: Squat form: setup, depth and the common faults
item.dc:creator: Diogo Camera
item.description: How to squat with good form: the setup step by step, how deep to go, whether your knees can pass your toes, the bar and dumbbell versions, and the faults.

item.title: Shoulder workout: three heads, three jobs
item.dc:creator: Diogo Camera
item.description: A shoulder workout for all three heads of the deltoid: the overhead press, lateral raises for the side, rows and reverse flies for the rear, gym or home.

item.title: How long to rest between sets: usually one to three minutes
item.dc:creator: Diogo Camera
item.description: How long to rest between sets: at least a minute for muscle growth, two to five for heavy compound lifts, less for small exercises, and how to time it.

item.title: Muscle soreness: how long it lasts, and whether to train through it
item.dc:creator: Diogo Camera
item.description: What delayed-onset muscle soreness (DOMS) is, how long it usually lasts, whether to work out when you're sore, and when soreness is a reason to see a doctor.

item.title: Leg day workout: a gym session and a dumbbell version
item.dc:creator: Diogo Camera
item.description: A leg day workout for the gym and a dumbbell version: the exercises for quads, hamstrings, glutes and calves, the sets and reps, and how often to train legs.

item.title: How to warm up before lifting: the sets before your sets
item.dc:creator: Diogo Camera
item.description: How to warm up before lifting: easy movement, then warm-up sets of your first lift. How many sets, at what weights, and dynamic vs static stretching.

item.title: How to do push-ups: from an incline to the floor, and past it
item.dc:creator: Diogo Camera
item.description: How to do push-ups with good form, how to start on an incline when the floor is too hard, how many to do, and the harder versions once twenty get easy.

item.title: How to do a pull-up: from zero to one, then more
item.dc:creator: Diogo Camera
item.description: How to do a pull-up with good form, and how to get your first one with negatives, bands, the assisted machine and the lat pulldown. Then how to add reps.

item.title: How many sets per week? Count hard sets per muscle
item.dc:creator: Diogo Camera
item.description: How many sets per muscle per week: 6 to 10 hard sets is plenty when you're new, 10 or more builds more muscle, and returns shrink past about 20.

item.title: How many reps per set? A wide range builds muscle
item.dc:creator: Diogo Camera
item.description: How many reps per set: about 6 to 15 is the efficient middle for muscle, heavier sets of 1 to 6 build more strength, and there is no magic hypertrophy range.

item.title: How active is your metro? The CDC's numbers for 48 big metros
item.dc:creator: Diogo Camera
item.description: 48 large U.S. metros in one table: adults reporting no physical activity in the past month and adults lifting twice a week, from the CDC's metro-area survey.

item.title: Hotel workout: one session for the room or the hotel gym
item.dc:creator: Diogo Camera
item.description: A full-body hotel workout for the room (no equipment) or the hotel gym (dumbbells), how to keep a travel week on track, and what a week off really costs.

item.title: Deload week: what it is, when to take one, and how
item.dc:creator: Diogo Camera
item.description: A deload week is a planned lighter week of lifting. What it is, how often lifters take one, how to cut sets or weight, and how it differs from a week off.

item.title: Deadlift form: learn the hinge, then pick your bar
item.dc:creator: Diogo Camera
item.description: How to deadlift with good form: learn the hip hinge first, then the conventional deadlift, the trap bar deadlift and the Romanian deadlift, and which to use.

item.title: Compound exercises: build the week on a few big lifts
item.dc:creator: Diogo Camera
item.description: What compound exercises are, the main movement patterns, how many to include, compound vs isolation exercises, and whether machines or free weights matter.

item.title: Commute times by state, and how to train around yours
item.dc:creator: Diogo Camera
item.description: The Census Bureau's average trip to work and work-from-home share for all 50 states and DC, with margins of error, and where training fits around each.

item.title: Chest workout: three exercises, counted by the week
item.dc:creator: Diogo Camera
item.description: A chest workout built on a flat press, a low incline press and a fly, about ten hard sets a week, with a gym and a home version and the studies behind it.

item.title: Cardio and lifting: order, timing and how much
item.dc:creator: Diogo Camera
item.description: Cardio before or after weights? Lift first if strength is the goal. Same day or separate days, how big the interference effect is, how much cardio, which kind.

item.title: A bodyweight workout: no equipment, full body, at home
item.dc:creator: Diogo Camera
item.description: A no-equipment bodyweight workout for beginners at home: a squat, hinge, push, pull and core move, an easier and harder version of each, and how to progress.

item.title: Bench press form: set up first, then add weight slowly
item.dc:creator: Diogo Camera
item.description: Bench press form step by step: the setup, how wide to grip, whether to arch, the rep itself, and how to increase your bench press without rushing it.

item.title: Back workout: pick a vertical pull, a row and a hinge
item.dc:creator: Diogo Camera
item.description: Build a back workout from three slots: a vertical pull, a horizontal pull and a hinge. Pick one from each, for the gym, machines and cables, or home.

item.title: Which workout split? Count your days first
item.dc:creator: Diogo Camera
item.description: Full body, upper/lower or push/pull/legs? Pick the workout split that fits the days you can train, then match your weekly sets. What the research says.

item.title: Rest days: how many you need, and what to do on them
item.dc:creator: Diogo Camera
item.description: How many rest days a week you need, whether it's bad to work out every day, what a rest or active recovery day looks like, and how rest fits a 3- or 4-day plan.

item.title: A college workout routine: three days around your classes
item.dc:creator: Diogo Camera
item.description: A college workout routine built around your classes: three full-body sessions a week, a two-day version for exam weeks, and a plan for the whole semester.

item.title: The best time to work out: the one you can repeat
item.dc:creator: Diogo Camera
item.description: The best time to work out is the one you can repeat. What research says about morning vs evening lifting, how to pick your slot, and early-morning tips.

item.title: A 30-minute workout: the full-body session that fits
item.dc:creator: Diogo Camera
item.description: A 30-minute full-body workout for the gym or home: a short warm-up, a squat, then two pairs. When 30 minutes is enough, what to cut first, and how to progress.

item.title: A dumbbell workout plan: three days a week, at home
item.dc:creator: Diogo Camera
item.description: A three-day dumbbell workout plan for home: six movements a session, two to three sets, weights that feel too easy, and a four-week rule for adding more.

item.title: How active is your state? The CDC's numbers, all fifty
item.dc:creator: Diogo Camera
item.description: Every state and DC in one table: the share of adults who report no leisure-time activity and the share who lift two or more days a week, from the CDC's state survey.

item.title: Online fitness coach vs. personal trainer: which one do you need?
item.dc:creator: Diogo Camera
item.description: Online coaching vs a personal trainer, side by side: who writes the plan, form feedback, accountability, flexibility, and when each one wins. Honest about thin evidence.

item.title: Is an online fitness coach worth it?
item.dc:creator: Diogo Camera
item.description: An honest answer from a coach: what an online fitness coach adds, what the research shows, and who should wait before hiring one.

item.title: How to start lifting weights: the first four weeks
item.dc:creator: Diogo Camera
item.description: A beginner's first four weeks of lifting: six movements, two or three short sessions a week, weights that feel too easy, and exactly when to add more.

item.title: Nervous about the gym? Your first day, step by step
item.dc:creator: Diogo Camera
item.description: Nervous about your first day at the gym? Decide the workout first, keep it short and easy, know the etiquette basics and have a plan for when you feel watched.

item.title: What the first month of online coaching actually looks like
item.dc:creator: Diogo Camera
item.description: The first month of online fitness coaching, week by week: the questions, the first plan, the first weigh-ins, the first call, and what usually feels hard.

item.title: Getting back into training after a long break
item.dc:creator: Diogo Camera
item.description: After months off you keep more than you think, mostly strength. Start lighter than your old numbers, train two or three times a week and build back over six weeks.

item.title: What is online fitness coaching, and how does it work?
item.dc:creator: Diogo Camera
item.description: Online coaching is a personalized training plan on your phone, with practical nutrition guidance and a real coach checking in weekly. How it works and who it's for.

item.title: Progressive overload: the one rule behind every good program
item.dc:creator: Diogo Camera
item.description: Progressive overload means asking a little more of your muscles over time: more weight, reps or sets. How to apply it, how fast to add weight and what to do when you stall.

item.title: How to choose an online fitness coach: seven things to check
item.dc:creator: Diogo Camera
item.description: Seven things to check before you hire an online fitness coach: whether they ask about your life first, how they track progress, how often you'll talk and what they promise.

item.title: How long does it take to see results from working out?
item.dc:creator: Diogo Camera
item.description: For most people: strength usually improves first, measurable muscle around weeks 4 to 8, and visible fat loss often takes 8 to 12 weeks or more.

item.title: Can you lose fat and build muscle at the same time?
item.dc:creator: Diogo Camera
item.description: Losing fat and building muscle at the same time is realistic for more people than you'd think. What body recomposition takes: protein, lifting, a small deficit and time.

item.title: Why you keep starting over (and how to stop)
item.dc:creator: Diogo Camera
item.description: Starting over usually isn't a willpower problem. It's a system problem: decide ahead, shrink the plan for bad weeks, never miss twice, have a witness.

item.title: Why can't I lose fat? Six common reasons
item.dc:creator: Diogo Camera
item.description: Eating healthy but not losing weight? Six things I'd check first: portions, underestimated intake, weekends, steps, consistency and one-day weigh-ins.

item.title: Walking is the most underrated tool for fat loss
item.dc:creator: Diogo Camera
item.description: Don't jump to a big number. Start from the steps you already average, add a bit and hold it until it feels routine. Then raise it.

item.title: There's always 3 reps in reserve
item.dc:creator: Diogo Camera
item.description: Reps in reserve (RIR) is how many more good reps you could have done before failure. For most working sets, aim for about 1 to 3 in reserve.

item.title: How often should you train? Less than you think.
item.dc:creator: Diogo Camera
item.description: Once a week beats none. General fitness and fat loss are happy on two or three days a week. Pick the schedule you can repeat, then make it count.

item.title: The 80/20 approach: eat flexibly without wrecking your progress
item.dc:creator: Diogo Camera
item.description: About 80% of what you eat is filling, protein-rich, mostly unprocessed food. The other 20% is food you simply enjoy. Calories and protein still count.

item.title: Consistency beats motivation. Every time.
item.dc:creator: Diogo Camera
item.description: Motivation comes and goes, so plan for the days you don't feel like it: set days and times, a smaller workout on bad days, and never miss twice.

item.title: Calories and protein: the two numbers that matter most
item.dc:creator: Diogo Camera
item.description: If you lift, aim for 0.7 to 1 gram of protein per pound of bodyweight a day. For calories, estimate your maintenance, pick a direction and adjust.
